messages.author: c5d55b0fc9f27a05
messages.subject: select grouped dataframe issue (0.2 -> 0.3.0.2)
parts:
Hi,

With dplyr 0.2, the following works as expected:

> mtcars %>% group_by(am) %>% do(tail(., n=1)) %>% subset(select=c(mpg, cyl))

   mpg cyl
1 19.2   8
2 21.4   4

However, with dplyr 0.3.0.2, I get:

> mtcars %>% group_by(am) %>% do(tail(., n=1)) %>% subset(select=c(mpg, cyl))
Warning: namespace 'R6' is not available and has been replaced
by .GlobalEnv when processing object ''
Error: index out of bounds


Is this expected? What is the warning message of "R6" namespace about? Thanks!

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: select grouped dataframe issue (0.2 -> 0.3.0.2)
parts:
Try reinstalling the R6 package.

Also you could do:

mtcars %>% group_by(am) %>% slice(n()) %>% select(mpg, cyl)

Hadley

parts:
Hadley, thanks for your quick reply!

I'm trying to update from 0.2 to 0.3.0.2 because of some bugs that was fixed in the new version. We have a lot of code, to make sure that I get the same result, I installed 0.3.0.2 to a separate location and loaded it using require(dplyr, lib.loc='path/to/0.3.0.2'). Maybe that is causing the 'R6' namespace issue.

I tried the same example on a test machine with regular installation. I don't have the 'R6' namespace warning anymore. However it still says 'index out of bounds'. Is it supposed to work?

The 'select' verb works for both 0.2 and 0.3.0.2, although it included the grouping variable as an additional column. In general I want to make little or no code change if possible..
